claims.text: High-strain-rate loading of nanostructured AlxCoCrFeNi activates grain-boundary sliding and migration.
Grain-boundary sliding and migration synergistically couple with dislocation slip in nanostructured AlxCoCrFeNi.
This coupled mechanism lowers dynamic flow stress relative to coarse-grained AlxCoCrFeNi.
This coupled mechanism enhances ductility relative to coarse-grained AlxCoCrFeNi.
The controlled comparison uses composition- and phase-matched AlxCoCrFeNi samples with ultrafine grains of at most 100 nm versus coarse grains of 1–2 µm.
Single-phase AlxCoCrFeNi alloys can exist.
The comparison should be conducted at strain rates of approximately 10^2–10^3 s^-1 at room and modestly elevated temperatures.
Ultrafine-grained samples have a higher-density grain-boundary network and associated excess volume.
A high grain-boundary density facilitates grain-boundary sliding and migration under high-strain-rate loading.
Boundary-mediated deformation provides additional plastic-strain accommodation concurrently with conventional dislocation slip.
Dislocation processes contribute to deformation and strength in concentrated NiCoCr-family alloys.
Nanostructured samples will have reduced strain-hardening rates relative to the coarse-grained baseline during dynamic loading.
Nanostructured samples will retain high overall strength while showing enhanced ductility.
The predicted boundary-mediated behavior occurs below a grain size of approximately 200 nm.
Above approximately 200 nm, deformation transitions to conventional dislocation-mediated behavior.
Coarse-grained AlxCoCrFeNi deforms mainly by dislocation slip under the stated dynamic-loading conditions.
Coarse-grained AlxCoCrFeNi has higher flow stress and conventional strain hardening relative to nanostructured material under matched dynamic loading.
The hypothesis may cease to apply when phase transformations dominate or when thermal activation overwhelms grain-boundary processes.
The quantitative contribution of grain-boundary sliding relative to dislocation activity may vary with processing conditions.
Failure to observe the predicted stress, strain-hardening, or grain-boundary-motion differences in the controlled comparison would falsify the hypothesis.
